scope: Internal BRISC development reliability-policy governance; not clinical utility estimation

interpretation.review_cost: One unit represents manual inspection, decision, correction or rejection effort, and workflow delay.
interpretation.false_alarm_cost: One unit is the review effort for an acceptable prediction; no extra penalty is added.
interpretation.missed_failure_cost: Ten units encode the preference for additional review over silent acceptance of Dice < 0.50; this is not a clinical or monetary estimate.
interpretation.true_negative_cost: Zero additional policy cost for an acceptable result accepted normally.

assumptions: All mandatory reviews have equal relative cost.
Flagged cases receive competent review before downstream use.
Review prevents the silent-acceptance cost of a missed failure.
Failure severity and tumor category do not change the initial cost.
Reviewer capacity, delay variation, disagreement, and residual reviewer error are not modeled.
Internal BRISC validation prevalence is not assumed to equal clinical prevalence.
The weights are engineering preferences, not clinical utility, monetary, or patient-harm estimates.
limitations: The cost ratio is a development preference rather than a clinically elicited utility.
Threshold performance will be estimated on internal validation data and may change under different prevalence or workflow costs.
Equal costs across tumor types do not model the weaker glioma subgroup separately.
Clinical deployment requires prospective workflow and human-review validation.
